newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb existing home sales rose 9.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb existing home sales rose 9.0 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes rose 9.0 percent in February to a seasonably adjusted annual rate of 4.26 million units from a revised 3.91 million units in January, the National Association of Realtors said Thursday.
Wall Street economists had forecast February sales of 4.05 million units.
The February sales rate was up 5.2 percent from sales of 4.05 million in February last year.

The association said that a stable economy and relatively low interest rates helped boost the existing home sales rate to the second highest level on record.
The group's chief economist said he does not expect the Federal Reserve's recent decision to raise interest rates to cause a "notable decline" in home sales.
"The increase in mortgage rates won't be high enough to pull people out of the market or cause them to postpone purchasing decisions," NAR Chief Economist John Tucillo said.
